name: ClaimChain AI demonstration evaluation set
description: A small, manually curated set of claim cases used to demonstrate and evaluate the deterministic verification pipeline. Each case carries the evidence links a retrieval stage would have produced, so the whole evaluation runs offline through the real Stage 4 aggregation code. This is NOT a statistically representative benchmark: it is a transparent demonstration set, sized for a university project review.
curation: Hand-authored. Each case states the subclaims a decomposition would produce and the relationship each retrieved passage was judged to have. Expected verdicts were derived from the frozen agg-1.0.0 rules, not fitted to the output.

cases.claim_text: Using HTTPS makes a website completely secure.
cases.notes: The project's canonical example. Two subclaims hold, the absolute completeness claim does not.

subclaims.text: HTTPS encrypts data in transit between the browser and the server.
HTTPS protects against some classes of network attack.
HTTPS makes a website completely secure against all attacks.

cases.claim_text: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
cases.notes: A well-established physical fact with consistent supporting evidence.

subclaims.text: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure.
Sea level corresponds to standard atmospheric pressure.

cases.claim_text: The Great Wall of China is the only man-made object visible from space with the naked eye.
cases.notes: A widely repeated claim that is contradicted by astronaut accounts and optical physics.

subclaims.text: The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye.
The Great Wall is the only man-made object visible from space.

cases.notes: Contradicted by large epidemiological studies; the originating paper was retracted.

subclaims.text: Vaccination causes autism spectrum disorder.
Aspirin has analgesic properties.
Aspirin reduces the pain of tension headaches.

cases.claim_text: The Apollo 11 Moon landings were staged in a film studio.
cases.notes: Contradicted by physical evidence, independent tracking, and retroreflectors still in use.

subclaims.text: The Apollo 11 landing was filmed in a studio rather than on the Moon.

cases.notes: Coffee has a mild diuretic effect but still contributes to fluid intake. Two supporting subclaims against one contradicted absolute, so the score stays positive while a material part is refuted.

subclaims.text: Caffeine has a mild diuretic effect.
Coffee contributes to daily fluid intake.
Drinking coffee leaves a person net dehydrated.

cases.claim_text: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
cases.notes: Tall structures are struck repeatedly; the absolute 'never' is refuted.

subclaims.text: Lightning never strikes the same location more than once.

cases.claim_text: A private company will announce a breakthrough product next Tuesday.
cases.notes: No retrievable evidence bears on a future private announcement, so the system must abstain.

subclaims.text: A private company will announce a breakthrough product next Tuesday.

cases.claim_text: An unnamed researcher once measured a record in an unrecorded experiment.
cases.notes: The claim is constructed so that no source could settle it; abstention is the correct outcome.

subclaims.text: An unnamed researcher measured a record in an unrecorded experiment.

cases.claim_text: Regular exercise improves cardiovascular health, doubles lifespan, and prevents all disease.
cases.notes: Only one of three subclaims has usable evidence, so coverage is 0.3333, below the 0.50 floor. The system abstains rather than guessing from a third of the claim.

subclaims.text: Regular exercise improves cardiovascular health.
Regular exercise doubles human lifespan.
Regular exercise prevents all disease.

cases.claim_text: Remote work increases productivity for all employees.
cases.notes: Evidence is genuinely split, so neither side dominates and the result is mixed rather than misleading.

subclaims.text: Remote work increases productivity.
